description: memory.rs:434-443 `pub struct MemoryError(pub String)` and lib.rs:142-151 `pub struct MockError(pub String)` are the `Self::Error` types for the two backends. Both follow a primitive-obsession pattern: error context flattened into an arbitrary format-string, Display impl just delegates to the String, no variants, no machine-readable discriminator. — Idiomatic Rust for a library error type uses `thiserror` or a hand-rolled enum with structured variants (`SerializeFailed { source: serde_json::Error }`, `UnknownAccount { id: String }`, `DeserializeFailed { type_name: &'static str, source: serde_json::Error }`, etc.). Callers can then match on variants instead of substring-matching on Display output — which is exactly what the unknown_account test at memory.rs:1252-1259 has to do: `msg.contains("unknown account")`. That substring match is the smell. — Caveat: both types are scoped to reference/test impls and a downstream backend brings its own Error. But the workspace AGENTS.md positions `memory::MemoryBackend` as 'a documented, complete, source-readable implementation … to study'. Contributors copying this shape will inherit the stringly-typed error and the substring-match test pattern. Engineering impact: medium — error-variant discrimination is exactly the kind of decision that should be made once at the foundation and then propagated.
title: MemoryError and MockError are stringly-typed: pub String tuple field, no variants
